enzyme_name: unidentified ATP-driven L-lysine efflux transporter (model placeholder "JM_Cre_653")
organism_context: Chlamydomonas reinhardtii ("Cre") draft-model entry; no EC, no gene, no KEGG/MetaCyc cross-reference to resolve the protein
rationale: The entry is an un-annotated model-specific transport placeholder, so no protein can be named; the ATP->ADP stoichiometry implies a primary active (ABC-type) lysine exporter, and ABC transporters are multi-subunit assemblies (two nucleotide-binding plus two transmembrane domains/subunits), i.e. a complex rather than a fused bi/polyfunctional chain.
direction_note: Inorganic phosphate is missing from the products (ModelSEED status MI:O:-3/P:-1), but the ATP-hydrolysing sense is still unambiguous: a primary active transporter runs ATP + Lys[c] -> ADP + Pi + Lys[e], so ModelSEED's reverse call would have transport synthesising ATP, which ABC pumps do not do.

rationale: Mirror-image partner of rxn34132 (import rather than export); the entry names no protein, and the ATP-coupled stoichiometry only identifies it as a primary active (ABC-type) importer, which is a multi-subunit complex (substrate-binding protein plus two permease and two ATPase subunits), not a fused bifunctional enzyme.
direction_note: Pi is missing from the products (ModelSEED status MI:O:-3/P:-1); even so the ATP-hydrolysing direction is the only physiological one, so ModelSEED's reverse call is wrong.

enzyme_name: no dedicated enzyme known; coproporphyrinogen I is a type-I shunt product that aromatises to coproporphyrin I, and the characterised oxidase CgoX/HemY is defined on the III isomer
organism_context: type-I porphyrinogen shunt; no organism has a described coproporphyrinogen I-specific oxidase
rationale: Coproporphyrinogen I is the dead-end isomer of the porphyrin pathway and its conversion to coproporphyrin I is not assigned to any characterised protein (it occurs largely by autoxidation), so the catalysing enzyme cannot be named; whether the Firmicute CgoX accepts the I isomer has not been established.
direction_note: Both the enzymatic (CgoX) and spontaneous routes use O2 as the oxidant and are irreversible aromatisations; ModelSEED substitutes NADP for O2 (and uses one NADP for what is a six-electron oxidation, hence status CI:4), and that substitution is what makes the computed thermodynamics point backwards.

enzyme_name: coproporphyrinogen III oxidase, oxygen-dependent (CgoX, formerly HemY; EC 1.3.3.15)
organism_context: Firmicutes/Bacillaceae coproporphyrin-dependent heme branch (Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus); an oxygen-independent alternative, CgoN (YtpQ), performs the same step in some species
rationale: CgoX is a single-chain FAD-dependent oxidase that aromatises coproporphyrinogen III to coproporphyrin III using O2; its reported ability to also oxidise protoporphyrinogen IX is broadened substrate specificity for the identical six-electron aromatisation chemistry, not a second distinct catalytic activity, so it stays monofunctional.
direction_note: The physiological oxidant is O2 (reduced to H2O2), which makes the aromatisation irreversible forward; ModelSEED replaces it with six NADP for a six-electron (three-acceptor) oxidation, leaving status CI:-6, and that bogus redox partner is what produced the reverse call.

enzyme_name: dimethylallyltranstransferase (geranyl/farnesyl diphosphate synthase; short-chain trans-prenyltransferase), EC 2.5.1.1
organism_context: plastidial entry (abbreviation rxn365_p) in a plant/algal model; the step is shared by bacterial IspA and plant GPP/FPP synthases
rationale: The DMAPP + IPP head-to-tail condensation is run by a short-chain trans-prenyltransferase whose successive elongation steps (the EC 2.5.1.1 and EC 2.5.1.10 labels) occur processively in one active site, i.e. one catalytic activity with chain-length scope, not two; genuinely bifunctional terpene synthases are those fusing a prenyltransferase domain to a separate cyclase domain, which this is not.
direction_note: The product is written as (E)-geranyl monophosphate instead of geranyl diphosphate, so a whole phosphate is missing (ModelSEED status MI:H:-2/O:-3/P:-1); the real condensation releases PPi, which is then hydrolysed, making the forward direction effectively irreversible and ModelSEED's reverse call wrong.

enzyme_name: phenylacetyl-CoA dehydrogenase / phenylacetyl-CoA:acceptor oxidoreductase (PadBCD), EC 1.17.5.1
organism_context: Thauera aromatica and Aromatoleum aromaticum; anaerobic (denitrifying) phenylalanine/phenylacetate catabolism to benzoyl-CoA
rationale: The purified enzyme is a membrane-bound molybdenum-iron-sulfur complex of three separate subunits (93, 27 and 26 kDa), so under the multi-subunit exclusion it counts as monofunctional rather than bifunctional; preparations additionally hydrolyse CoA off phenylglyoxylyl-CoA, but that thioesterase activity was not assigned to a single polypeptide and lies beyond the step written here.
direction_note: The four-electron alpha-oxidation inserts a water-derived oxygen and is a committed catabolic step with no observed reverse; the reverse call comes from the generic MetaCyc "acceptor" being instantiated as the plant quinone phylloquinone (vitamin K1) rather than the physiological ubiquinone, which is what set the eQuilibrator dG.

enzyme_name: thiosulfate:quinone oxidoreductase (TQO, DoxDA), EC 1.8.5.2
organism_context: Acidianus ambivalens (thermoacidophilic Sulfolobales); homologous DoxDA systems in Acidithiobacillus caldus and other sulfur oxidisers
rationale: The purified holoenzyme consists of two distinct polypeptides, DoxA (28 kDa) and DoxD (16 kDa), so it is a two-subunit complex and not a fused bifunctional chain; that the same two subunits also occur in the terminal quinol:O2 oxidoreductase (cytochrome aa3) is complex sharing, not a second catalytic activity on one chain.
direction_note: TQO physiologically oxidises thiosulfate to tetrathionate and passes the electrons to caldariella/sulfolobus quinone and on to O2, which pulls the marginal couple forward; the entry instantiates the generic quinone as phylloquinone (vitamin K1) and omits the O2-reducing sink, and that is what made the computed dG favour the reverse.

enzyme_name: thiosulfate:quinone oxidoreductase (TQO, DoxDA), EC 1.8.5.2
organism_context: Acidianus ambivalens (Sulfolobales); same enzyme as rxn35651, only the instantiated quinone differs
rationale: Same two-subunit DoxA/DoxD membrane complex as rxn35651, with no cofactors beyond the non-covalently bound quinone mixture; separate polypeptides mean the multi-subunit exclusion applies and the enzyme is monofunctional.
direction_note: The acceptor here is instantiated as the one-electron radical p-benzosemiquinone for a two-electron thiosulfate oxidation (ModelSEED status CI:1), a non-physiological partner; the real reaction is quinone reduction feeding O2 respiration, which runs thiosulfate -> tetrathionate forward.

enzyme_name: no enzyme identified for this exact pair; nominal parent is the generic EC 1.1.1.71 NAD(P)-dependent alcohol dehydrogenase. In conifers the real diterpenol -> diterpenal oxidation is done by the cytochrome P450 abietadienol/abietadienal oxidase PtAO (CYP720B1) and its CYP720B relatives, not by an NAD(P) dehydrogenase.
organism_context: conifer (Pinus taeda, Picea spp.) diterpene resin acid biosynthesis
rationale: This is a MetaCyc generic-reaction combinatorial expansion (".metaexp.") that pairs levopimaradienol with isopimaradienal, i.e. a different diterpene skeleton, while the matching aldehyde levopimaradienal (cpd25390) exists separately in the database, so no characterised protein runs the written conversion. CYP720B1, the enzyme that actually performs the conifer diterpenol oxidations, is called multifunctional in the literature but applies one monooxygenase chemistry iteratively to several substrates.
direction_note: NAD-linked alcohol/aldehyde interconversion is near-equilibrium, so direction is set by the NAD+/NADH pool rather than by the enzyme; in the real pathway the step is instead an irreversible O2/NADPH-dependent P450 oxidation.

enzyme_name: none - no enzyme catalyses the written conversion; the nominal parent is the generic EC 1.2.1.5 NAD(P)-dependent aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH)
organism_context: conifer diterpene resin acid context for the substrate (abietal); the fatty-acid product belongs to a different pathway entirely
rationale: A MetaCyc generic-reaction combinatorial expansion (".metaexp.") pairs the tricyclic C20 diterpene aldehyde abietal with the unrelated saturated straight-chain fatty acid arachidate, with seven bare H+ padded in to force an atom balance (ModelSEED status CI:-10); no single enzyme performs this, so the catalyst cannot be named.
direction_note: Read as the intended ALDH chemistry (diterpene aldehyde -> the corresponding diterpenoic acid), the oxidative direction is effectively irreversible because the acyl-enzyme is hydrolysed; ALDHs do not reduce carboxylates (that requires an ATP-dependent carboxylic acid reductase), so ModelSEED's reverse call is wrong whatever the product mis-pairing.
